skill.name: seo-audit
skill.description: Audits website SEO across crawlability, indexation, technical health, on-page elements, content quality, international targeting, and site-specific issues.
skill.summary: Diagnose SEO problems and turn evidence into a prioritized action plan.

The skill contains no executable scripts, shell commands, credential handling, or prompt injection. Its network guidance points only to an example domain and Google's Rich Results Test.

content.user_title: Audit Your Website SEO and Prioritize Fixes
content.value_statement: SEO problems can hide across crawling, metadata, content, performance, and international targeting. This skill organizes evidence into clear findings and a prioritized action plan.
actual_capabilities: Reviews crawlability, indexation, robots directives, XML sitemaps, canonicals, redirects, and site architecture.
Assesses Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, HTTPS, URL structure, and common performance factors.
Checks titles, meta descriptions, headings, keyword targeting, internal links, images, and content depth.
Diagnoses hreflang, locale canonicals, international sitemaps, locale URLs, and translation quality.
Adapts checks for SaaS, e-commerce, blogs, multilingual sites, and local businesses.
Produces evidence-based findings with impact, fixes, priorities, quick wins, and longer-term actions.
limitations: It cannot access Search Console, analytics, or paid tools unless the user provides access or exports.
Static fetch tools cannot confirm JavaScript-injected schema markup; use a browser or Rich Results Test.
Findings depend on the supplied URLs, crawl data, business context, and target keywords.
It audits structured data but directs implementation work to a dedicated schema skill.

use_cases.title: Recover SaaS Search Traffic
use_cases.description: Diagnose ranking losses after a migration, release, or search update, then prioritize recovery work.

use_cases.title: Control E-commerce Crawl Waste
use_cases.description: Review faceted navigation, duplicate product pages, crawl budget, pagination, and out-of-stock handling.

use_cases.title: Validate International SEO
use_cases.description: Check hreflang clusters, locale canonicals, multilingual sitemaps, translated content, and locale URL consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic SEO Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [URL] for technical, on-page, and content SEO issues. Ask for missing context, then rank findings by impact and effort.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a first review of one website.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Ranking Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why [page URL] is not ranking for [keyword]. Review intent, metadata, depth, indexation, canonicals, internal links, and cannibalization.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when one page remains below expected rankings.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Traffic Decline
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the traffic decline after [migration or release]. Use provided Search Console data, redirects, canonicals, robots directives, sitemaps, and URL changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after a site change or sudden organic decline.

prompt_templates.title: Audit International SEO
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [site] across [locales]. Validate reciprocal hreflang, self-canonicals, x-default, sitemap alternates, locale URLs, translated content, and conflicting signals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for complex multilingual or multi-regional websites.

output_examples.input: Audit our SaaS site after a WordPress to Next.js migration.
output: Critical: Several legacy URLs lack direct permanent redirects to matching new pages.
High: New pages publish inconsistent canonicals, which can delay index recovery.
Next steps: repair redirects, align canonicals, submit the new sitemap, and monitor Search Console coverage.

output_examples.input: Review our multilingual store for international SEO problems.
output: High: French pages reference English canonicals, which can suppress French indexing.
Medium: Several hreflang clusters lack reciprocal links and an x-default fallback.
Next steps: add self-canonicals, repair reciprocal annotations, and validate sitemap alternates.

output_examples.input: Why is our product page stuck on page three for its target keyword?
output: High: The page title and primary heading target different search intents.
Medium: Two related pages compete for the same keyword and receive stronger internal links.
Next steps: consolidate intent, strengthen supporting content, and revise internal link destinations.

best_practices: Provide priority URLs, target keywords, recent site changes, competitors, and current traffic context.
Share Search Console exports, crawl reports, and analytics evidence when available.
Validate JavaScript-rendered schema with a browser, Rich Results Test, or rendering crawler.
anti_patterns: Do not report missing schema from static fetch output alone.
Do not recommend fixes without evidence, impact, priority, and affected URLs.
Do not treat every SEO checklist item as equally urgent.

faq.question: Can this skill audit an entire website?
faq.answer: Yes, when crawl data or representative URLs are available. The audit quality and coverage depend on the evidence provided.

faq.question: Does it need Search Console access?
faq.answer: No. Search Console data improves indexation, query, and traffic analysis, but the skill can begin with public pages.

faq.question: Can it diagnose a sudden traffic decline?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the decline date, affected sections, recent releases, migrations, redirects, and available Search Console or analytics data.

faq.question: Does it check Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews LCP, INP, CLS, and common causes involving servers, images, JavaScript, CSS, caching, fonts, and CDNs.

faq.question: Can it verify structured data?
faq.answer: It can review rendered structured data. Static fetch results alone are insufficient for schema injected by client-side JavaScript.

faq.question: Does it support multilingual websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks hreflang reciprocity, self-canonicals, x-default, international sitemaps, locale URLs, and translated content quality.
